body:

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 9:07 AM PST
Subject: Re: [P1] Optimize Suggestions API p95 latency regression (prod) — investigation + mitigation plan

FYI: PagerDuty fired for /optimize/suggestions p95. This is impacting Console Suggestions page load times (and in some cases table never fully populates).

Initial hypotheses (based on last week’s rollout + query patterns):
1) DB query path regressed (N+1, missing index, or overly expensive default sort)
2) Payload size / expensive joins when returning details fields for list view
3) Cache miss + concurrency spike from beta accounts refreshing / paging

Plan for next 60–90 min:
- Follow runbook and pull traces/logs to identify dominant spans.
- Confirm whether regression correlates with any recent deploy(s) to suggestions-service.
- If we can’t get p95 < 500ms quickly, mitigation will be to (a) temporarily disable the Suggestions view for non-dogfood orgs via feature flag and/or (b) degrade response (list-only fields, no expanded explanations) until we ship a fix.

References:
- Runbook: sources/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/runbook-suggestions-api-latency-and-error-triage.json
- Recent related PRs:
  - sources/github/redwood/pr-21934-add-optimize-suggestions-api-contract.json
  - sources/github/redwood/pr-22063-suggestions-compute-job-retries-and-staleness.json

I’ll update by 10:30 with findings + a concrete mitigation recommendation.

— Dylan
Engineering (Console & Tooling)
Redwood Inference

Thanks. For mitigation, I’m aligned with degrading/flagging off the Suggestions entry point for beta accounts if needed — but please keep internal dogfood enabled so we can validate fixes.

Also: if you think the Console is accidentally polling too aggressively, we can ship a quick UI tweak to reduce refresh frequency (we just turned on a “sort by savings” default and some folks are paginating a lot).

Keep me posted.

Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 9:36 AM PST
Subject: Re: [P1] Optimize Suggestions API p95 latency regression (prod) — investigation + mitigation plan

+1 on keeping dogfood on.

User impact note: this is the exact thing that erodes trust in the beta (people interpret slow/empty as “no data” or “estimates are made up”). If we need to degrade the response, can we ensure the UI shows a clear banner like “We’re experiencing slowness; data may load gradually” instead of falling into the “insufficient telemetry” empty state?

Also, if you can tag whether the latency is on list vs details drawer endpoint (or list w/ expanded fields), that will help us decide what to cut first.

— Aditya
-----

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 11:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: [P1] Optimize Suggestions API p95 latency regression (prod) — findings + mitigation

Update (root cause + immediate steps):

Findings:
- The latency is dominated by the list endpoint query path (not the details drawer). The slowest span is DB time on suggestion list retrieval when sorting by estimated savings.
- We’re seeing an N+1-ish pattern when hydrating per-suggestion “explanations / input signals” fields even when the Console is only rendering the table.
- Correlates with the default sort change + increased paging (beta accounts doing “sort by savings” + filter toggles).

Mitigation (effective now):
1) Console-side: I’m asking Marissa’s team to avoid requesting expanded fields in list view (list should only fetch summary columns). This should cut payload size and the extra joins.
2) Server-side: we can add a short-term guard to not join explanation blobs for list responses unless include_details=true.
3) Feature flag: if p95 is still > 800ms after (1)/(2), we should temporarily turn off Suggestions for the 3 noisiest beta orgs while we patch the query. (Dogfood stays on.)

Fix in progress:
- There is already a PR addressing the query pattern and removing the N+1 behavior:
  - sources/github/redwood/pr-22079-fix-n-plus-one-in-suggestions-query.json
  I’m reviewing now and will push for an expedited merge + deploy after verifying it doesn’t change API shape.

UX note (Aditya): agree. If we do flag off, we should show a “temporarily unavailable” banner, not “insufficient telemetry.” That’s a different state.

Next update at ~12:30 after PR review + canary.

— Dylan
-----

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 2:27 PM PST
Subject: Re: [P1] Optimize Suggestions API p95 latency regression (prod) — mitigation applied + status

Status update: mitigation applied, regression contained.

- Deployed query optimization change (includes the N+1 removal) from:
  - sources/github/redwood/pr-22079-fix-n-plus-one-in-suggestions-query.json
- Added a server-side check to only hydrate “why/explanations” fields when include_details=true.
- Console is being adjusted to request summary-only for list view; Marissa’s note about reducing refresh/paging is still a good follow-up, but not required for p95 recovery.

Current metrics (last 20 min):
- /optimize/suggestions p95: ~380–430ms (down from ~1.9s)
- 5xx: back to baseline (<0.2%)

No need to disable beta orgs at this point.

Follow-ups (to prevent repeat):
- Add a perf test that exercises “sort by savings + pagination” and asserts query count (no N+1).
- Document the “list vs details” field contract more explicitly (so UI doesn’t accidentally request heavy fields).
- Add an alert on DB query count / time for this endpoint, not just wall latency.

If we see another spike overnight, next rollback lever is to temporarily force default sort to “most recent” instead of “highest savings” until we confirm index coverage.

— Dylan
